Lina to share tracing quickstart doc and sandbox link
Customer to provide sample failing request ids for debugging
action_items: Samir Patel - Send pricing and pilot guide - 2028-09-21
Lina Torres - Share tracing quickstart and console links - 2028-09-16
Mark Chen - Provide 3 example request IDs and a repro script - 2028-09-18

summary: Walkthrough of Redwood Console tracing, error analysis, and request logs with focus on debugging flows for production incidents. Covered how to correlate traces to request logs, use filters, download full request payloads, and tie logs to auditing/KMS controls. Agreed next steps: pricing, sandbox access, and sample request IDs from Horizon.
questions: How do we correlate trace ids with request logs?
What level of PII is stored in logs and how is it redacted?
Can we push logs to our SIEM?
What are the latency impacts of tracing?
transcript:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Samir on the account team, with Lina and Diego from SE. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Aisha Singh: Good thanks, quick context — we run Horizon payments infra, and we're evaluating Redwood for inference on several customer-facing flows, most urgent is debugging production anomalies in our chat summarization pipeline.
[00:22] Samir Patel: Perfect, today we'll focus on the Console tracing and request logs, show how you can drill into errors and debug. Lina will demo.
[00:30] Lina Torres: Great, jumping in — opening the Console, this is the tracing tab, you'll see a list of recent traces, each trace maps to a request lifecycle. Note: sometimes trace ids show up as t-... or  a UUID, transcription might show it odd.
[01:05] Mark Chen: Quick q — can we correlate these to our own request ids? We append our request_id header.
[01:12] Lina Torres: Yes, you can set request headers to be indexed; we can search by header or by trace id. I'll show filters — header:client-request-id:abc123 — this filters trace list.
[01:30] Lina Torres: Clicking a trace, you get timeline with spans: router, model selection, kv-cache lookup, and the actual token generation span. You can expand spans to see metadata including latency, GPU node, and any exceptions.
[02:05] Rachael Lee: How does this impact PII? Are request payloads stored raw?
[02:12] Diego Ramos: Good question — by default we persist request logs with redaction rules you configure; full payloads can be retained in Dedicated/Private with your KMS, for Hosted we redact by default and provide options. We'll share security docs.
[02:40] Aisha Singh: Is there an easy way to download the full request for a trace?
[02:45] Lina Torres: Yes, on the trace detail there's a 'Download request' button, which gives you the original request JSON and server response, but download availability depends on your retention policy and account type.
[03:05] Samir Patel: I'll note that for the pilot we can enable extended retention in the sandbox so you can test downloads.
[03:20] Mark Chen: We sometimes see intermittent 500s — can tracing show root cause?
[03:28] Lina Torres: Absolutely, we'll replicate a 500 scenario — watch the error span, it surfaces stack traces or runtime error codes and the associated logs table below. Often you'll see a model OOM or a kernel fallback in the notes.
[03:50] [screen share noise] Lina Torres: I'm going to filter traces for errors only, then group by model type to see if a particular model variant is spiking.
[04:12] Mark Chen: Looks like model-x-qa pops up a lot.
[04:16] Lina Torres: Right — next step you can drill into request logs for a problematic trace and see token-by-token timings and exact payload.
[04:30] Rachael Lee: Can those logs be exported to our Splunk or Datadog?
[04:35] Diego Ramos: Yes, we have log forwarding — you can push request logs and traces to an external sink via our integrations or via S3 export then to SIEM. We'll provide the integration guide.
[04:55] Aisha Singh: On compliance — SOC 2, and we use customer-managed KMS, need audit logs for key usage. How does Redwood handle that?
[05:05] Samir Patel: For Private and Dedicated, you can use your own KMS and we emit key usage logs; for Hosted we integrate with external KMS via secure links — details are in the security packet.
[05:20] Rachael Lee: Any RBAC around who can download request payloads?
[05:24] Lina Torres: Yes, Console has RBAC and SSO (SAML/OIDC) roles — you can require specific role to access downloads, and all downloads are logged in audit trail.
[05:40] Mark Chen: Can tracing add our internal trace ids? We use Zipkin style trace correlation.
[05:45] Lina Torres: You can inject your traceparent or a header and we will propagate. We also ship an SDK snippet that attaches our trace id to your logs for easy correlation.
[06:05] [slight cross talk] Mark Chen: Ok show us an end-to-end debug flow.
[06:12] Lina Torres: Sure — step 1: find failing trace via the 'Errors' filter, step 2: open span timeline, step 3: check the request logs table which lists the request/response pairs and any server-side warnings, step 4: click 'Download request', step 5: copy request id into your local repro and run against the sandbox.
[06:45] Lina Torres: I'm highlighting a trace now — see this error span here, the annotation says 'kv-cache miss then retried' and a subsequent spike in token latency.
[06:58] Mark Chen: Interesting, could be cold-start or cache invalidation.
[07:02] Lina Torres: Right. Also note the 'Model Fallback' annotation — if a node is out of capacity we fallback to a quantized variant which can increase latency or change responses. You can set automatic fallback policies in the routing config.
[07:25] Aisha Singh: How do we set routing policy per environment?
[07:30] Diego Ramos: In the Console under 'Routes' you can create policies scoped to stage/prod. For pilot we recommend a canary route for say 10% of traffic and enable fallback for low-latency tier.
[07:48] Samir Patel: Also worth calling out batching effects — sometimes increased batching for cost can change tail latency; tracing helps you see per-token latencies so you can tune batch size.
[08:05] Mark Chen: Can we see GPU node id to check whether it's a hot node?
[08:10] Lina Torres: Yes, span metadata includes node id and region, plus kernel selection notes. If we see one node repeatedly failing we can route away.
[08:25] Rachael Lee: On retention — what are default retention windows for request logs?
[08:30] Diego Ramos: Hosted default is 30 days with redaction; Dedicated/Private can be configured up to whatever your contract allows. We can set longer retention for pilot if needed.
[08:45] [pause] Lina Torres: I'm going to show the 'Error analysis' view — you can group errors by signature or by route and pin a golden trace as a reference for regressions.
[09:05] Mark Chen: Can those signatures be exported to our monitoring alerts?
[09:10] Lina Torres: Yep — you can wire up regression alerts to notify Slack or PagerDuty and link back to trace.
[09:20] Aisha Singh: Do you keep diffs of model outputs for quality monitoring?
[09:25] Diego Ramos: Redwood Optimize includes quality monitoring tied to prompt sets; we track output regressions and can point to traces where outputs diverged. That's an add-on we can demo separately.
[09:40] Mark Chen: Let's dig into a real 500 — Rachael, you had an example earlier?
[09:44] Rachael Lee: Yes, we captured a few request ids in last week's incident (I'll paste in chat).
[09:50] [chat noise] Mark Chen: Pasting id r-2028-0910-01 now.
[09:55] Lina Torres: Great — searching... here it is. Opening trace, you can see the token gen span threw 'model OOM' and the response was a 500.
[10:12] Mark Chen: What does model OOM mean operationally? Does it indicate memory leak?
[10:18] Diego Ramos: Usually OOM indicates a request pushed beyond the configured sequence length or a node with fragmentary memory. We'll check kernel logs; Console shows node metrics and pre/post GC events when available.
[10:30] Lina Torres: Notice also the 'request size' in metadata — this was 2.4x our normal median, which likely triggered the fallback.
[10:40] Aisha Singh: Wouldn't fallback avoid 500s?
[10:44] Lina Torres: Fallback tries to route to compatible variant but sometimes the variant accepts different sequence lengths; fallback config can be tuned to prefer availability over fidelity.
[10:55] Samir Patel: For the pilot we can run a load test with varied sizes to ensure fallback policies behave as you'd like.
[11:05] Mark Chen: Can we simulate cache behavior? Cold vs warm?
[11:10] Lina Torres: Yes — enable prefix caching in sandbox and you can mark requests as cacheable; tracing will show hits vs misses in span annotations.
[11:22] Rachael Lee: Are span annotations exportable? We want to ingest them into our APM.
[11:26] Diego Ramos: Yes exports include span metadata; we support OTLP/Zipkin exporters.
[11:35] Mark Chen: About log redaction — if we need raw non-redacted logs for debugging, is there an audit path?
[11:42] Lina Torres: For Hosted we have a process: temporary elevated access with strict audit and redaction exceptions; for Dedicated/Private you can retain raw logs with your KMS.
[11:55] Aisha Singh: What about egress of logs — is there PII leakage risk when forwarding to third-party SIEM?
[12:02] Diego Ramos: You control what fields are forwarded, we recommend scrubbing sensitive fields before export. We can add a pre-export transform rule.
[12:15] Mark Chen: Let's talk about severity-based alerting.
[12:20] Lina Torres: In Error Analysis you can create alert rules by error signature, rate, or latency threshold. Each alert can contain a link to a trace set and a query snapshot for reproducibility.
[12:35] Samir Patel: Do you want us to show alert wiring to your Slack/PagerDuty next call?
[12:40] Aisha Singh: Yes, please.
[12:42] Rachael Lee: On the security side, one more ask: we need proof of key rotation practices and whether Redwood keeps any plaintext keys.
[12:50] Samir Patel: We'll include our KMS and key rotation docs in the security packet. For Hosted we never store your plaintext keys; Dedicated/Private give you full control.
[13:05] Mark Chen: Any network requirements for forwarding logs or using the tracing agent?
[13:10] Diego Ramos: Agent needs outbound to our ingestion endpoints; for Private we can peering or private link. We'll share the network checklist.
[13:22] Lina Torres: Now moving to request logs view — it's a tabular view with columns: timestamp, request_id, route, model, status, latency, and a preview of request. You can expand row to full payload and even replay the request to a sandbox endpoint.
[13:40] Mark Chen: Replay — does that hit production models?
[13:43] Lina Torres: Replay can be targeted at sandbox or at production read-only mode; for writes or stateful interactions you should use sandbox. Replay headers are tunable so you can re-run under identical conditions.
[13:58] Aisha Singh: For replays do you preserve client headers so we can reproduce auth flows?
[14:05] Diego Ramos: You can preserve or override headers, and we recommend overriding auth and pointing to a test identity.
[14:18] Mark Chen: Is there rate limit on replay?
[14:20] Lina Torres: Replays are rate-limited to avoid accidental floods; limits depend on plan.
[14:30] [brief pause] Lina Torres: I'm going to demo a replay of a failing request to the sandbox showing we can reproduce the 500 locally.
[14:42] [typing/screen click sounds] Lina Torres: Replay succeeded in sandbox but we see the same memory spike — I'll attach kernel log snippet here in the console.
[14:58] Mark Chen: Do you surface kernel-level logs in Console or is that separate?
[15:03] Diego Ramos: We surface summarized kernel logs and a link to raw logs if available under the node diagnostics panel. Full raw kernel logs are typically reserved for Dedicated/Private or by support request.
[15:18] Rachael Lee: Can we get a daily export of traces metadata for trend analysis?
[15:24] Lina Torres: Yes, you can schedule exports to S3 or push them to your observability pipeline. We'll include an example config.
[15:40] Mark Chen: For pilot we'd want 2 weeks of extended retention and replay enabled — can you accommodate?
[15:46] Samir Patel: Yes, we can provision that in a sandbox pilot. I'll include in the pilot proposal.
[15:55] Aisha Singh: Pricing question — is tracing an add-on or included?
[15:59] Samir Patel: Basic tracing and request logs are included on hosted plans up to standard retention; extended retention, exports, and Optimize integrations are add-ons. Pricing details in the proposal.
[16:15] Mark Chen: How do we control who can run replays? We need approvals.
[16:20] Lina Torres: RBAC + approval workflow — you can require an approval step before a replay or restrict replays to specific roles. It's in the policy section.
[16:35] Rachael Lee: Are audit logs immutable? We need tamper evidence.
[16:40] Diego Ramos: Audit logs are append-only and we timestamp and sign events; for Dedicated/Private you can ship them to your own immutable store as well.
[16:55] Samir Patel: I'll drop the security packet link in the chat after the call.
[17:02] Lina Torres: Next I'll show error grouping — we can see this regression surfaced last week and group by signature. You can pin a baseline trace and then every new trace is compared via diff.
[17:25] Mark Chen: That diff—does it show token-level differences?
[17:28] Lina Torres: Yes token-level diffs are supported in Optimize add-on. The error analysis will show diffs in the response and you can mark false positives.
[17:45] [brief cough] Aisha Singh: We need to validate that model fallback doesn't change policy outputs — is there a way to assert invariants?
[17:54] Diego Ramos: You can run assertions as part of routing test suites; Optimize can run these checks and alert on regressions.
[18:08] Mark Chen: Any latency overhead to enabling tracing?
[18:12] Lina Torres: Minimal — tracing adds small headers and instrumentation; token generation path is mostly unaffected. Heavy sampling can add overhead, but you can tune sampling rate per route.
[18:30] Rachael Lee: Sampling rate defaults?
[18:33] Lina Torres: Default 10% for hosted, you can increase for specific routes.
[18:42] Samir Patel: We'll propose a pilot config with 100% sampling for a narrow test route so you can debug comprehensively.
[18:54] Mark Chen: Can we redact certain fields at ingest time?
[18:58] Lina Torres: Yes, ingestion transforms can redact fields and we can apply regex or JSON path rules.
[19:10] Mark Chen: If we redact, can we still replay?
[19:13] Diego Ramos: Redaction is permanent on those fields unless you keep raw logs in Dedicated/Private. For replay you need the raw request; so for debugging we recommend storing raw logs in a secured bucket with KMS and limited access.
[19:30] Aisha Singh: Okay makes sense.
[19:35] Lina Torres: I'm going to show integration with PagerDuty — hooking an alert to a runbook with a direct trace link.
[19:44] [screen show] Lina Torres: When you open an alert it shows top traces, top affected routes, and a link 'Create Incident' which pre-populates the incident with trace and request ids.
[20:02] Mark Chen: That's useful. Can incidents be annotated by our ops folks?
[20:06] Lina Torres: Yes, incidents support comments and attachments; everything gets surfaced in the audit trail.
[20:15] Rachael Lee: On the topic of model variants — you mentioned we can pin versions per route?
[20:20] Diego Ramos: Correct, pin to a specific model version and roll out variants via canary or A/B. The Console tracks performance per variant.
[20:33] Mark Chen: If a canary starts failing, can we auto-rollback?
[20:36] Lina Torres: Yes, you can set automatic rollback policies based on error rate or latency SLOs.
[20:45] Samir Patel: Since we're close to time, I'll quickly recap and call out next steps.
[20:50] Samir Patel: 1) Samir to send pricing and pilot proposal, 2) Lina will share tracing quickstart and sandbox link, 3) Mark to send sample request IDs, 4) schedule follow-up to wire alerts to PagerDuty.
[21:10] Aisha Singh: That works. Anything else from you, Rachael?
[21:15] Rachael Lee: Please include KMS and key rotation docs and examples of audit logs.
[21:20] Samir Patel: Will do.
[21:25] Mark Chen: One last nit — how do you handle multi-tenant logs? We want strict tenant separation.
[21:30] Diego Ramos: For Hosted we partition logs and enforce RBAC; Dedicated/Private gives physical separation. We'll diagram this in the security packet.
[21:45] Aisha Singh: Thanks, helpful demo.
[21:48] Samir Patel: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up by EOD with links.
[21:52] [call wrap up noise] Lina Torres: I'll drop the sandbox link, quickstart, and the trace export example.
[22:00] Samir Patel: Thanks all, talk soon.
[22:05] [END]
